gbm_population_evidence.quote: Diagnosis of recurrent or progressive glioblastoma, WHO Grade IV, IDH wild-Type or astrocytoma WHO grade IV.

candidate_evidence.quote: In this study we are evaluating the safety and feasibility of the triple combination (TTFields, MLA, pembrolizumab) in adult patients diagnosed with recurrent or progressive glioblastoma (GBM) WHO Grade IV, IDH wild type or recurrent or progressive astrocytoma WHO grade IV.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Diagnosis of recurrent or progressive glioblastoma, WHO Grade IV, IDH wild-Type or astrocytoma WHO grade IV.

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Patients randomized to treatment arm 1 will start treatment with Optune GIO® for 3-7 days and undergo MLA and biopsy for tumor diagnosis and immune monitoring.
Patients randomized to treatment arm 2, will start treatment with Optune GIO® for 3-10 days and receive one infusion of pembrolizumab before undergoing MLA/biopsy.

role_evidence.quote: Keytruda® is the trade name for pembrolizumab, which will be given as 200mg IV Q3 weeks. This treatment will continue for up to two years.
Number of participants experiencing a DLT after receiving the triple combination (TTFields, MLA, pembrolizumab) in adult patients diagnosed with recurrent glioblastoma from both arms

arms: Arm 1: Optune GIO® pre-MLA; MLA; followed by Optune GIO® + Pembrolizumab post MLA
Arm 2: Optune GIO®+Pembrolizumab pre-MLA; MLA; followed by Optune GIO® + Pembrolizumab post MLA

source_quote.quote: Diagnosis of recurrent or progressive glioblastoma, WHO Grade IV, IDH wild-Type or astrocytoma WHO grade IV.

coder_notes: Eligibility allows 'astrocytoma WHO grade IV' without an IDH requirement (historical GBM per D27C) alongside IDH-wildtype glioblastoma; coded gbm_only, cns5_terminology cns5 because IDH-wildtype is required for glioblastoma (both criteria met). Pembrolizumab is the only drug; TTFields (Optune GIO) and MRI-guided laser ablation (NeuroBlate) are devices, not agents, and are not radiotherapy, so regimen coded monotherapy by the manual definition although the tested intervention is a drug-device triple combination. Pembrolizumab is not described as needing the devices for delivery/activation, so device_dependent false. Both arms are experimental and differ only in timing of pembrolizumab relative to MLA/biopsy. Biopsy for 'immune monitoring' after pre-MLA pembrolizumab in Arm 2 suggests a pharmacodynamic comparison, but no immune endpoint is registered and the link to pembrolizumab is not stated, hence target_engagement_planned unclear. IDH-wildtype is diagnostic only.
